meta.title: Ballade No. 1 - Moderato Theme Study (6/4 Lilt)
meta.composer_source: Study after Frederic Chopin, Ballade No. 1 Op. 23 mm. 8-23

theory.summary: Trains the iconic 6/4 barcarolle-waltz accompaniment and singing G-minor melody of Ballade No. 1.
theory.pattern_tip: Hear each 6/4 bar as two graceful three-beat groups: bass on beat 1, warm inner chord on beat 2, breath on beat 3.
theory.technique_tip: Keep the left hand light and buoyant on the bass-to-chord leaps so the right-hand cantabile melody floats above.
theory.ballade_link: Direct rhythmic, harmonic (i -> iv -> V7/V -> V7 -> bII6 -> i6/4 -> V7 -> i), and textural bridge to Op. 23 mm. 8-23.
theory.concept_title: 6/4 Barcarolle Lilt & Synthesis of Op. 23 Harmony
concept_paragraphs: Welcome to the summit of Selfano's curriculum! Here the opening Moderato of Ballade No. 1 unites everything you built across Tiers 1-6: the G-minor key signature (Tier 3), wide bass-to-chord leaps (Tier 2/5), secondary V7/V & V7/VI modulations (Tier 4), and the tragic bII6 -> i6/4 -> V7 -> i finale (Tier 6).
Feel the 6/4 meter not as six heavy beats, but as two three-beat barcarolle sighs per bar: rich bass root on beat 1, warm mid chord on beat 2, and weightless breath on beat 3.

form_map.role: Singing Moderato opening gently alternating Tonic Gm (i) and Dominant D7 (V7).
Climbs through Cm (iv) and bright A7 (V7/V) into heartfelt D7 resolution.
Opens into warm Eb (VI) and Bb (III) via F7 (V7/VI) before darkening again.
Summits through the Neapolitan Ab/C (bII6) -> Gm/D (i6/4) -> D7 -> Gm cadence.

practice_steps: 1. Map the 16-bar harmony first in Chord Skeleton mode, spotting A7 (Bar 6) and Ab/C (Bar 14).
2. Keep LH 6/4 accompaniment undulating smoothly—beat 1 anchors, beat 2 cushions, beat 3 breathes.
3. Play the RH melody alone singing out every half-step sigh before combining hands.
4. Progress calmly from 60% through 80% up to 96 BPM.
